key_insight: Introduce content-aware, motion-adaptive caching for Diffusion Transformers that updates cached intermediate features based on perceptual drift instead of treating them as static snapshots, enabling fast inference without ghosting or blur.
problem_solved: Diffusion Transformers for video world models are slow due to sequential denoising and expensive spatio-temporal attention; prior training-free caching methods reuse features as static snapshots (Zero-Order Hold), causing ghosting, blur, and motion inconsistency when global drift is non-negligible.
method: Content-aware caching: detect perceptual or motion-driven drift and decide when and where to refresh cached features (per-frame / per-region) rather than holding them fixed.
Lightweight correction modules: apply cheap residual/warp/interpolation updates to cached activations to compensate for motion-induced changes, preserving detail without full recomputation.
Training-free, plug-and-play integration: designed to work with existing DiT-based video world models and denoising pipelines to accelerate inference while maintaining visual fidelity.
impact: Significantly reduces inference compute and latency for high-fidelity video world models while avoiding common caching artifacts, enabling more efficient development and deployment of video prediction, simulation, and real-time world modeling systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: DiT denoising loop with content-aware cache layer and correction module highlighted.
Before/after frame comparison: demonstration of ghosting/blur with static caching vs cleaned output with content-aware updates.
Compute vs quality chart: inference latency or FLOPs on x-axis vs perceptual/video quality on y-axis showing improved trade-off.
Cache policy schematic: per-frame / per-patch decision flow (detect drift → update/warp/hold) illustrated with icons for motion, cache, and correction.
paper_title: WorldCache: Content-Aware Caching for Accelerated Video World Models
paper_authors: Umair Nawaz, Ahmed Heakl, Ufaq Khan, Abdelrahman Shaker, Salman Khan
